searchvalues-repeated-membership-search.title: Reuse SearchValues<T> for repeated membership searches
searchvalues-repeated-membership-search.short: Precompute a search set used across many span scans
searchvalues-repeated-membership-search.summary: SearchValues<T> represents a reusable set optimized for repeated IndexOfAny-style searches over spans.
searchvalues-repeated-membership-search.why: Parsers and text processors often scan many buffers for the same delimiters, where rebuilding the search representation wastes work.
searchvalues-repeated-membership-search.tips: Create the SearchValues instance once for a stable set and benchmark realistic inputs before replacing simple one-off searches.

frozen-collections-read-mostly-lookups.title: Use frozen collections for read-mostly lookup tables
frozen-collections-read-mostly-lookups.short: Pay construction cost once for lookup-heavy immutable data
frozen-collections-read-mostly-lookups.summary: FrozenDictionary and FrozenSet build immutable lookup structures optimized for repeated reads after construction.
frozen-collections-read-mostly-lookups.why: Routing tables, keyword sets, and application metadata can trade slower setup for efficient steady-state lookup.
frozen-collections-read-mostly-lookups.tips: Build them after the source data is final; use normal mutable collections when updates remain part of the workload.

valuetask-asynccache-fast-path.title: Use ValueTask for measured synchronous async fast paths
valuetask-asynccache-fast-path.short: Avoid a Task allocation when an async result is commonly already available
valuetask-asynccache-fast-path.summary: ValueTask<T> can represent either an immediately available value or asynchronous work without always allocating a Task<T>.
valuetask-asynccache-fast-path.why: Very hot cache and I/O abstractions may benefit when successful synchronous completion is common and profiling shows Task allocation matters.
valuetask-asynccache-fast-path.tips: Do not adopt it by default; callers must respect ValueTask consumption rules and the extra complexity must justify the gain.

async-hotpath-unnecessary-task-allocatio.title: Avoid unnecessary async state machines on synchronous hot paths
async-hotpath-unnecessary-task-allocatio.short: Do not add async and await when a method only forwards an existing task
async-hotpath-unnecessary-task-allocatio.summary: An async wrapper can add state-machine and continuation overhead when it merely awaits and returns an already available task result.
async-hotpath-unnecessary-task-allocatio.why: Tiny helpers called at high frequency can accumulate avoidable async overhead without improving cancellation or error handling.
async-hotpath-unnecessary-task-allocatio.tips: Keep async when try/finally, exception timing, using scopes, or additional awaits require its semantics; optimize only measured hot paths.

pipereader-buffer-lifetime.title: Respect PipeReader buffer lifetime boundaries
pipereader-buffer-lifetime.short: Do not retain sequence memory after advancing the reader
pipereader-buffer-lifetime.summary: Memory exposed by PipeReader belongs to the pipeline and should be treated as invalid for later use after AdvanceTo releases it.
pipereader-buffer-lifetime.why: Holding slices beyond their valid lifetime can produce subtle corruption or force unnecessary retention of pooled buffers.
pipereader-buffer-lifetime.tips: Finish parsing before AdvanceTo or copy only the data that truly must outlive the current read.

socket-pipelines-backpressure.title: Apply pipelines backpressure to streaming network parsers
socket-pipelines-backpressure.short: Consume only processed bytes and let bounded buffering slow producers
socket-pipelines-backpressure.summary: System.IO.Pipelines coordinates producers and consumers through owned buffers and AdvanceTo positions, enabling streaming parsers to express consumption.
socket-pipelines-backpressure.why: Network readers can avoid unbounded buffering when incoming data arrives faster than application processing.
socket-pipelines-backpressure.tips: Advance examined and consumed positions accurately and set thresholds based on protocol message sizes rather than arbitrary large buffers.

eventsource-eventcounter-diagnostics.title: Expose runtime diagnostics with EventSource and counters
eventsource-eventcounter-diagnostics.short: Publish low-level events and measurements for diagnostic tooling
eventsource-eventcounter-diagnostics.summary: EventSource integrates application events and counters with .NET runtime diagnostic infrastructure and collection tools.
eventsource-eventcounter-diagnostics.why: Libraries and services can expose operational signals without coupling their core code to one monitoring backend.
eventsource-eventcounter-diagnostics.tips: Keep event schemas stable, avoid sensitive payloads, and prefer System.Diagnostics.Metrics when metric interoperability is the primary goal.

aspnetcore-output-caching.title: Cache HTTP responses with ASP.NET Core output caching
aspnetcore-output-caching.short: Reuse eligible endpoint responses under explicit cache policies
aspnetcore-output-caching.summary: ASP.NET Core output caching stores selected HTTP responses and can serve later matching requests without recomputing endpoint work.
aspnetcore-output-caching.why: Read-heavy endpoints can reduce repeated database, rendering, and serialization cost when their responses have safe cache semantics.
aspnetcore-output-caching.tips: Define variation and expiration deliberately and never cache user-specific or authorization-sensitive responses under a shared key.

reflection-create-delegate-fast-invocati.title: Compile repeated reflection calls into delegates
reflection-create-delegate-fast-invocati.short: Resolve a MethodInfo once and invoke through a typed delegate
reflection-create-delegate-fast-invocati.summary: MethodInfo.CreateDelegate turns a resolved method into a delegate that can be reused instead of repeatedly performing reflective invocation.
reflection-create-delegate-fast-invocati.why: Frameworks that discover handlers through reflection can keep dynamic discovery while making repeated calls cheaper and strongly typed.
reflection-create-delegate-fast-invocati.tips: Cache delegates by a stable key and validate signatures during setup so failures happen before the hot path.

unity-component-lookup-hot-path.title: Cache Unity component lookups used every frame
unity-component-lookup-hot-path.short: Resolve stable component references outside Update loops
unity-component-lookup-hot-path.summary: Repeated component discovery in Update or other high-frequency callbacks performs work that is unnecessary when the component relationship is stable.
unity-component-lookup-hot-path.why: Many objects performing repeated lookups can consume frame time even though each individual call appears small.
unity-component-lookup-hot-path.tips: Cache only references whose lifetime is actually stable and refresh them when components can be replaced dynamically.
